title: Florida AI Laws

reading.body:
Florida's only AI-related law is a resolution recognizing Tampa Bay as a cybersecurity and AI innovation region, not a rule that binds anyone.

The single enacted measure, S1816, passed on 2026-03-12 and does no more than acknowledge CyberBay, affirm the state's cybersecurity posture, and endorse public-private collaboration. It creates no obligations, no disclosure duties, and no compliance burden for developers or operators. A reader looking for Florida's actual constraints on AI will not find them here.

That absence is the point. Florida has not yet regulated AI through statute, so any AI build in the state faces no state-level legal requirement captured by this data. The practical constraint on Florida data centers and the power they draw remains federal, local, and utility-level, none of which this page covers.

What this data does not tell you is whether Florida has AI-relevant rules outside enacted legislation, such as agency guidance, executive orders, or pending bills. It tracks one law, read from enrolled text, and nothing else.

Enacted AI laws in Florida

1 law this site judged relevant to AI, newest first, each read from its enrolled text.

  • S1816: CyberBay passed 2026-03-12

    The Florida Senate recognizes CyberBay as a cybersecurity and artificial intelligence innovation region within the Tampa Bay area, acknowledges Florida's national leadership in cybersecurity preparedness and digital defense, and affirms the importance of continued public-private collaboration to strengthen cyber readiness and economic resilience.

How this page is kept

This page is generated from the enacted laws this site tracks for Florida. When the legislature passes another AI-related bill, it appears here the night the bill's text is read. The full 50-state picture is at State AI Laws.
